intent: Trace cumulative confirmed COVID-19 deaths worldwide from March 2020 through March 2021 and quantify the overall change.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
Does the video trace the cumulative confirmed COVID-19 deaths worldwide from March 2020 through March 2021 and quantify the overall change?
The overall change in global cumulative confirmed COVID-19 deaths from the start (0.00 million) to March 2021 (2.50 million) is an increase of 2.50 million deaths.

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: Global cumulative confirmed COVID-19 deaths increased monotonically from 0.00 million at the start (point_order 1) to 2.50 million by March 2021, passing through 0.28M (April), 0.52M (June), 0.78M (Aug), 1.00M (Sept), 1.35M (Nov), and 1.95M (Jan).
units.computation: Check that the series values are non-decreasing in point_order: 0.00, 0.28, 0.52, 0.78, 1.00, 1.35, 1.95, 2.50 (million).
accept: The line rises continuously from the start to March 2021.
All listed intermediate values are shown or implied in order.
reject: Omitting the start or end point of the traced period.

units.claim: The overall change in global cumulative confirmed COVID-19 deaths from the start (0.00 million) to March 2021 (2.50 million) is an increase of 2.50 million deaths.
accept: The overall increase is quantified as 2.50 million.
The change is described as an increase from 0 to 2.5 million.
reject: Describing the change as a decrease or no change.

optional_valid: Mentioning that the cumulative deaths reached 1.00 million by September 2020.
Noting that the increase accelerated in the later months (e.g., from 1.35M in Nov to 2.50M in March 2021).
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for the increase (e.g., variants, vaccination rollout) not present in the table.
Comparing to other countries or regions not in the data.
Exact daily or weekly values between the listed anchor points.
review_notes: The table includes an initial point with empty x and point_order 1, value 0.00; it is treated as the start of the traced period.
The intent asks to trace the trend and quantify the overall change; two semantic units cover these operations.
No cross-panel comparison is needed because there is only one panel.
